report.summary: Main already lets a run start when a login file is missing: commit f1b8a67 (#63) treats the SDK's ENOENT (file not found) as absent, and a test in runs.cases.ts covers it. This diff goes further and treats every readFile error as an absent file. Errors like permission denied, an I/O error, the container not being reachable or a timeout now hash as null. The guard on protected login and config files used to fail with RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION when it couldn't check a file. Now it lets the run through, which weakens a security control the spec keeps 'as today' (08 §244). The change also has no test for the new behavior and no spec or implementation-notes update.

findings.text: `.catch(() => null)` treats every read error as 'file absent', so the guard no longer fails when it can't check a file. Ways to slip past it: (1) the agent writes a protected file that didn't exist before, such as ~/.gitconfig or ~/.codex/config.toml, and makes it unreadable to the reader. The before hash is null and the after read throws EACCES, which also becomes null, so nothing is flagged. (2) A container or SDK error during the before snapshot and again after the turn records null both times, which hides any change in between. (3) A one-off read failure on a file that exists records null at start, then a good read after the turn shows a change that didn't happen. Before this diff, every non-ENOENT error raised RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION ('could not be checked'), and runs.ts:450 still expects that path. Keep the `SandboxFileError.is(cause) && cause.code === "ENOENT"` narrowing, and add any other codes that really mean 'not there' (e.g. ENOTDIR) one by one instead of catching everything.

The request ('a login the owner never set up must not block a run') is already met on main: #63 handles ENOENT, and runs.cases.ts has 'runs when a login file is missing, as for an owner without a Codex login'. Nothing in the diff shows a login that was never set up producing a different error. If one does (e.g. a different SDK code for a missing parent directory), name that code and add a test that reproduces it rather than catching every error.

The change in behavior comes with no test (CLAUDE.md rule 14). There should be a test asserting that a read error other than ENOENT (e.g. EACCES, or the container being unreachable) still fails the run with RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION. A test showing the new behavior would have made the security regression obvious.

The spec says protected-file checks continue 'as today', and errors.ts describes RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION as a security failure. Changing whether the check fails when it can't read a file needs a spec or IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES change in the same PR (CLAUDE.md rules 1 and 16). Silently letting unreadable files pass is new behavior the spec doesn't describe.

args.command: cat apps/tempo/src/agents/protected-files.ts; grep -rn "protectedFileHashes\|RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION" --include=*.ts --include=*.md . | grep -v node_modules | head -40
args.description: Read changed file and find usages

args.command: git log --oneline -3; git diff --stat HEAD~1 2>/dev/null | tail -3; grep -rn -i "protected\|ENOENT" docs/*.md docs/IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md | head -20; grep -rn -i "protected\|ENOENT\|readFile" apps/tempo/test | head -20
args.description: Check spec and tests for protected files
